question: Should experiment-gated Claw lifecycle diagnostics become a supported core Doctor contribution after the state-read defect is fixed, or should the broader Claws direction remain outside core pending RFC sponsorship?
rationale: The implementation adds a new core lifecycle-management and diagnostic surface rather than repairing a current documented behavior; repository policy requires maintainer judgment for broader product and ownership direction.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core diagnostic slice
options.body: Keep the read-only Doctor contribution in core after restoring WAL-aware migration detection and establishing a clear support boundary for the experiment.

options.title: Pause the core lifecycle stack
options.body: Defer these diagnostics until maintainers accept the Claws RFC and define the permanent owner and compatibility contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core diagnostic slice
recommendation.body: Keep the read-only Doctor contribution in core after restoring WAL-aware migration detection and establishing a clear support boundary for the experiment.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review identified the relevant live-state and read-only observation contract, making them the strongest available routing candidate from the supplied discussion.
